key_insight: A phone-based chatbot can deliver trustworthy maternal health information in low-resource settings by handling short, code-mixed queries and combining regional, context-specific grounding with safety-aware triage.
problem_solved: Addresses the technical and safety challenges of giving reliable maternal health advice over phone chat where users have low health literacy, use code-mixed language, provide underspecified symptom information, and require region-specific guidance and safe routing.
method: Design and implement a phone-ready chatbot pipeline that handles short, underspecified, and code-mixed user queries (language identification + normalization).
Ground responses in region-specific maternal health guidance and integrate a safety/triage module to detect red flags and route users to urgent care when needed.
Evaluate the system with human-centered metrics (user comprehension, trust, safety) and stakeholder feedback (care providers, local users) to validate real-world utility.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building safe, grounded, multilingual health chatbots for low-resource contexts—highlighting data collection, grounding, and triage as critical components for trustworthy deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: input (code-mixed short query) → language processing → grounding to regional guideline → safety/triage decision → user response
Chat example card: a real-style short, code-mixed user query and the chatbot's grounded, safe reply (before/after clarification)
Evaluation snapshot: simple bar or radar chart showing key metrics (safety detection rate, user trust/satisfaction, clarification frequency)
Icon set: phone/low-bandwidth, language/code-mix, shield for safety/triage, map/region for local grounding
paper_title: Developing and evaluating a chatbot to support maternal health care
paper_authors: Smriti Jha, Vidhi Jain, Jianyu Xu, Grace Liu, Sowmya Ramesh
